sanity_expectations: omega(t) is monotone increasing during the spin-up and approaches a finite steady plateau (no runaway, no oscillation)
bearing_temp(t) is monotone increasing and approaches a finite plateau; heating tracks omega^2 during the transient
domega_dt(0) = drive_torque / inertia = 10 rad/s^2 (positive, largest at t=0)
domega_dt(t) decays smoothly toward 0 as omega approaches the child's steady-state plateau
the child's steady-state omega is slightly LOWER than the parent's (thermal-expansion drag adds an extra loss channel)
bearing_temp remains bounded (cooling eventually balances heating) and stays much smaller than 1/friction_temp_coeff so the viscous-friction feedback does not blow up
all outputs stay real and finite over t in [0, 800] s
excitation_report: Full-system child-vs-parent comparison over t in [0, 800] s. The new term -thermal_expansion_drag*bearing_temp*omega/inertia reaches a max effect on the omega(t) trajectory of 7.92*sigma (peaks near t ~ 744 s, once the bearing has heated substantially and omega has approached its plateau). Established terms (drive, viscous friction, quadratic drag, static-friction/tanh, windage-heating coupling, and the parent's temperature-dependent friction) all dominate at least one region of the transient and thus each contribute far more than 5*sigma to domega_dt; the parent system reaches a well-behaved plateau in omega and bearing_temp, and the child settles to a slightly lower plateau because of the thermal-expansion drag. sigma = 0.005 rad/s^2 on the domega_dt label.
role_corrections: omega: dynamic state (confirmed, integrated first-order state under the domega_dt RHS)
bearing_temp: dynamic state (confirmed, second integrated state governed by its own thermal ODE)
thermal_expansion_drag: P->P (confirmed, fixed at 1e-2, upper end of the suggested 1e-5..1e-2 range, needed so the new mechanism clears 5*sigma within physically reasonable bounds)
rationale: Structure agrees with the upstream contract: two coupled first-order ODEs in (omega, bearing_temp), so equation_type=ode_system and integrator=integrate_system; state_variables, state_rhs, initial_conditions and rhs_for_integrator are inherited verbatim. analyze_expression on the target RHS confirmed no derivatives, no integral kernels and no ungoverned functions of t: the only symbols are (omega, bearing_temp) and the eleven fixed parameters. Parameters were chosen for a physically stable spin-up: drive_torque=10 N.m against friction_coeff=0.05 N.m.s/rad and quad_drag_coeff=5e-4 gives a parent plateau near omega ~ 100 rad/s; heat_capacity=5 J/K with cooling_coeff=0.1 W/K makes the bearing warm noticeably during the transient (needed for the new term to bite), while friction_temp_coeff=5e-4 /K keeps the viscous-friction feedback safely below runaway. thermal_expansion_drag is fixed at 1e-2 (upper edge of the suggested 1e-5..1e-2 range) so the new mechanism -thermal_expansion_drag*bearing_temp*omega/inertia is genuinely visible above noise: excitation_check reports 7.92*sigma at t~744 s. check_substitution at a representative interior point (omega=100, bearing_temp=20) evaluates to a finite real number, confirming the RHS stays well-defined over the sampling region. Sampling is 400 linearly spaced points on t in [0, 800] s so we capture both the initial spin-up transient and the slow thermal drift where the new term becomes strongest.
